  - `subtract` boolean, Length and puff the other way: shorten, flatten
- `particleEdit.stroke` (writes): Grooms hair along `points` with a brush.
  - `kind` string, one of `comb` | `cut` | `length` | `puff` | `smooth`, The grooming brush
  - `points` json[], required, The stroke's path: [x, y] viewport pixels
  - `radius` number, Radius in viewport pixels (50)
  - `strength` number, Strength, 0 to 1 (0.5)
  - `subtract` boolean, Length and puff the other way: shorten, flatten
- `presence.local` (reads): Shares this person's pointer and selection with collaborators; answers what it shares.
  - `pointer` integer[], The pointer in viewport pixels [x, y]; left out when it left the view
- `presence.peers` (reads): Tells the editor where other people's pointers and selections are, for drawing them.
  - `peers` json, required, presence/peers as the host sent it
- `presence.place` (reads): Answers where to draw other people's pointers in the viewport. No parameters.
- `curve.set` (writes): Changes curve `object`: dimensions, resolution, extrude, bevel depth and resolution, fill, cyclic.
  - `bevelDepth` number, The radius of the round profile swept along the curve, metres
  - `bevelResolution` integer, Segments in each quarter of the bevel's profile (4)
  - `cyclic` boolean, Close every spline on itself
  - `dimensions` string, one of `2d` | `3d`, 2d keeps the curve flat and fills closed splines
  - `extrude` number, Half the height the curve is extruded to, metres
  - `fillCaps` boolean, Close the ends of an open bevelled curve
  - `fillMode` string, one of `full` | `half` | `both` | `front` | `back` | `none`, 3D: full or half profile; 2D: which faces fill a closed curve
  - `object` integer or string, The curve or text; the active or edited one when left out
  - `offset` number, Moves the curve along its normals, metres
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
  - `resolution` integer, Samples per segment, for every spline (12)
- `text.set` (writes): Changes text `object`: body, font size, alignment, extrude, bevel, spacing.
  - `align` string, one of `left` | `center` | `right`, Horizontal alignment of each line
  - `bevelDepth` number, The round edge's radius, metres
  - `bevelResolution` integer, Segments in the round edge (4)
  - `body` string, The text; a newline starts a new line
  - `characterSpacing` number, Letter spacing as a multiple of each advance (1)
  - `extrude` number, Half the thickness the letters are extruded to, metres
  - `font` string, The font's name (only the bundled Inter is available)
  - `lineSpacing` number, Line distance as a multiple of the size (1)
  - `object` integer or string, The curve or text; the active or edited one when left out
  - `offsetX` number, Moves the text sideways, metres
  - `offsetY` number, Moves the text up, metres
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
  - `resolution` integer, Points per curved segment of each letter (12)
  - `shear` number, Slants the letters: x moves by shear × y
  - `size` number, The text's size (1: the font's full height is one metre)
  - `wordSpacing` number, Space width as a multiple (1)
- `curve.setSplines` (writes): Replaces the splines of curve `object` with `splines` (points, handles, cyclic).
  - `object` integer or string, The curve or text; the active or edited one when left out
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
  - `splines` json[], required, Splines as {type: bezier|poly|nurbs, points: [{co: [x,y,z], left?, right?, leftType?, rightType?: auto|vector|aligned|free, radius?, tilt?, weight?}], cyclic?, resolution?, order?, endpoint?}; Bézier handles left out are automatic
- `curve.select` (reads): Selects curve points by index in curve edit mode.
  - `deselect` boolean, Take them out of the selection
  - `extend` boolean, Add to the selection
  - `points` integer[], Control points, counted through the splines in order (handles go with their point)
- `text.caret` (reads): Moves the caret in text edit mode by `by`, to `to`, or to a place (start, end, line start, …) and answers it.
  - `by` integer, Characters to move (negative: back)
  - `place` string, one of `start` | `end` | `lineStart` | `lineEnd` | `up` | `down`, A place to go
  - `to` integer, A character index
- `lattice.set` (writes): Changes lattice `object`: resolution and interpolation, or resets its points.
  - `interpolation` string, one of `bspline` | `linear`, How the points' offsets blend (bspline)
  - `object` integer or string, The lattice; the active or edited one when left out
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
  - `reset` boolean, Put every point back where it rests
  - `resolution` integer or array, Points along each side, 1 to 64: one number for all three, or [u, v, w]
- `lattice.movePoints` (writes): Moves lattice points (by index, else the selected ones) by `offset`.
  - `object` integer or string, The lattice; the active or edited one when left out
  - `offset` number[], required, How far to move them, in the lattice's own axes [x, y, z]
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
  - `points` integer[], Point indices (u + v × U + w × U × V); the selected points in edit mode when left out
- `lattice.select` (reads): Selects lattice points by index in lattice edit mode.
  - `deselect` boolean, Take them out of the selection
  - `extend` boolean, Add to the selection
  - `points` integer[], Point indices
- `nodes.removeGroup` (writes): Deletes node group `group`.
  - `group` integer or string, The group's id or name; the only group when left out
- `nodes.renameGroup` (writes): Renames node group `group`.
  - `group` integer or string, The group's id or name; the only group when left out
  - `name` string, required, The new name
- `nodes.addNode` (writes): Adds a node of `kind` (see `nodes.describe`) to `group` at `location` with input `values`.
  - `group` integer or string, The group's id or name; the only group when left out
  - `kind` string, required, one of `groupInput` | `groupOutput` | `group` | `repeatInput` | `repeatOutput` | `simulationInput` | `simulationOutput` | `meshCube` | `meshGrid` | `meshUvSphere` | `meshIcoSphere` | `meshCylinder` | `meshCone` | `meshLine` | `meshCircle` | `curveLine` | `curveCircle` | `curveBezierSegment` | `curveQuadrilateral` | `curveSpiral` | `curveStar` | `curveToMesh` | `curveToPoints` | `fillCurve` | `resampleCurve` | `trimCurve` | `reverseCurve` | `setCurveRadius` | `setCurveTilt` | `setSplineType` | `setNurbsOrder` | `setNurbsWeight` | `setSplineCyclic` | `setSplineResolution` | `splineParameter` | `curveLength` | `endpointSelection` | `transform` | `joinGeometry` | `setPosition` | `deleteGeometry` | `mergeByDistance` | `subdivideMesh` | `subdivisionSurface` | `extrudeMesh` | `meshToPoints` | `meshToCurve` | `distributePointsOnFaces` | `pointsToVertices` | `instanceOnPoints` | `realizeInstances` | `setMaterial` | `storeNamedAttribute` | `captureAttribute` | `position` | `normal` | `index` | `value` | `vector` | `objectInfo` | `separateXyz` | `combineXyz` | `math` | `vectorMath` | `randomValue` | `compare` | `switch` | `mapRange` | `sceneTime` | `namedAttribute` | `domainSize` | `attributeStatistic` | `accumulateField` | `meshBoolean` | `dualMesh` | `flipFaces` | `splitEdges` | `triangulate` | `scaleElements` | `meshIsland` | `edgeAngle` | `faceArea` | `edgeNeighbors` | `sampleIndex` | `sampleNearest` | `raycast` | `geometryProximity` | `translateInstances` | `rotateInstances` | `scaleInstances` | `instanceRotation` | `instanceScale` | `rotateEuler` | `rotateRotation` | `rotateVector` | `eulerToRotation` | `rotationToEuler` | `axisAngleToRotation` | `invertRotation` | `renderLayers` | `image` | `rgb` | `compositorOutput` | `viewer` | `alphaOver` | `brightContrast` | `colorBalance` | `exposure` | `hueSaturation` | `invert` | `mixColor` | `rgbCurves` | `blur` | `denoise` | `glare` | `defocus` | `vectorBlur` | `kuwahara` | `cryptomatte` | `chromaKey` | `colorKey` | `differenceKey` | `distanceKey` | `keying` | `luminanceKey` | `ellipseMask` | `lensDistortion` | `crop` | `flip` | `rotate` | `scale` | `imageTransform` | `translate` | `materialOutput` | `textureCoordinate` | `geometryInfo` | `fresnel` | `layerWeight` | `principledBsdf` | `diffuseBsdf` | `glossyBsdf` | `glassBsdf` | `transparentBsdf` | `emission` | `volumeAbsorption` | `volumeScatter` | `principledVolume` | `mixShader` | `addShader` | `imageTexture` | `noiseTexture` | `voronoiTexture` | `gradientTexture` | `checkerTexture` | `waveTexture` | `colorRamp` | `separateColor` | `combineColor` | `mapping` | `bump` | `normalMap`, The node's kind (nodes.describe lists their sockets)
  - `location` number[], [x, y] in the editor's units
  - `values` object, Socket and setting values by id, as nodes.setValue takes them
- `nodes.removeNodes` (writes): Removes nodes by index from `group`.
  - `group` integer or string, The group's id or name; the only group when left out
  - `nodes` integer[], required, The nodes' ids
- `nodes.moveNodes` (writes): Moves nodes of `group` to `location` or by `offset` in the node editor.
  - `group` integer or string, The group's id or name; the only group when left out
  - `location` number[], [x, y] to put the (one) node at
  - `nodes` integer[], required, The nodes' ids
  - `offset` number[], [dx, dy] to move each by
- `nodes.setValue` (writes): Sets input or property `id` of node `node` in `group` to `value`.
  - `group` integer or string, The group's id or name; the only group when left out
  - `id` string, required, An input socket's or a setting's id
  - `node` integer, required, The node's id: its id
  - `value` json, The value: a number, [x, y, z], a boolean, a setting's choice, an object or material id, a text; null clears it
- `nodes.link` (writes): Links output socket `fromSocket` of node `from` to input socket `toSocket` of node `to` in `group`.
  - `from` integer, required, The node whose output to link: its id
  - `fromSocket` string, required, The output socket's id
  - `group` integer or string, The group's id or name; the only group when left out
  - `to` integer, required, The node whose input to link: its id
  - `toSocket` string, required, The input socket's id; a link already there is replaced unless the input takes several
- `nodes.unlink` (writes): Removes the link between two sockets in `group`.
  - `from` integer, Only the link from this node: its id
  - `fromSocket` string, Only the link from this output socket
  - `group` integer or string, The group's id or name; the only group when left out
  - `to` integer, required, The node whose input to unlink: its id
  - `toSocket` string, required, The input socket's id
- `nodes.addInput` (writes): Adds an input socket of `type` to node group `group`'s interface.
  - `default` json, The value a modifier uses when it sets none
  - `group` integer or string, The group's id or name; the only group when left out
  - `name` string, required, The input's name, unique in the group
  - `type` string, required, one of `geometry` | `float` | `int` | `bool` | `vector` | `rotation` | `object` | `material` | `string`, What the input carries
- `nodes.removeInput` (writes): Removes input `name` from node group `group`'s interface.
  - `group` integer or string, The group's id or name; the only group when left out
  - `name` string, required, The input's name
- `nodes.addOutput` (writes): Adds an output socket of `type` to node group `group`'s interface.
  - `group` integer or string, The group's id or name; the only group when left out
  - `name` string, required, The output's name, unique in the group (a Group node using the group gives it)
  - `type` string, required, one of `geometry` | `float` | `int` | `bool` | `vector` | `rotation`, What the output carries
- `nodes.removeOutput` (writes): Removes output `name` from node group `group`'s interface.
  - `group` integer or string, The group's id or name; the only group when left out
  - `name` string, required, The output's name
- `nodes.addZoneItem` (writes): Adds an item to a repeat or simulation zone node's state.
  - `group` integer or string, The group's id or name; the only group when left out
  - `name` string, required, The item's name, unique in the zone: a socket on both of its nodes
  - `node` integer, required, Either node of the zone: its id
  - `type` string, required, one of `geometry` | `float` | `int` | `bool` | `vector` | `rotation`, What the item carries
- `nodes.removeZoneItem` (writes): Removes an item from a repeat or simulation zone node's state.
  - `group` integer or string, The group's id or name; the only group when left out
  - `name` string, required, The item's name
  - `node` integer, required, Either node of the zone: its id
- `nodes.describe` (reads): Lists the node kinds a tree takes (or one `kind`) with their inputs, outputs and properties, for `nodes.addNode`.
  - `group` integer or string, The group's id or name; the only group when left out
  - `kind` string, One kind; every kind when left out
  - `tree` string, one of `geometry` | `compositor` | `shader`, Only the kinds a geometry, a compositing, or a shader group takes
- `compositor.set` (writes): Turns compositing on or off and sets which group renders use.
  - `compositing` boolean, Whether renders pass through the group
  - `group` integer or string or null, The compositing group renders pass through: its id or name; null for none: its id or name
- `compositor.setImage` (writes): Sets the image an image node of the compositing group reads (workspace path or base64).
  - `base64` string, The image file's bytes, base64
  - `clear` boolean, Take the node's picture away
  - `group` integer or string, The compositing group (the one renders use when left out): its id or name
  - `image` string, An image the scene has already, by its hash
  - `name` string, The image's name, with base64
  - `node` integer, required, The Image node's id
  - `path` file, An image file (PNG, JPEG, or Radiance HDR) to read
- `compositor.pickMatte` (writes): Adds the name under `x`, `y` of the render to a Cryptomatte node's matte (or takes it away with `remove`).
  - `group` integer or string, The compositing group (the one renders use when left out): its id or name
  - `node` integer, required, The Cryptomatte node's id
  - `remove` boolean, Take the name away from the matte instead (false)
  - `x` number, required, Across the render, 0 (left) to 1 (right)
  - `y` number, required, Down the render, 0 (top) to 1 (bottom)
- `compositor.preview` (reads): Answers the compositing group's result (or a viewer node) as a picture of `size`.
  - `group` integer or string, A compositing group to preview other than the render's: its id or name
  - `size` integer, The longer side of the preview in pixels, 16 to 2048 (480)
  - `viewer` boolean, Answer what the Viewer node shows instead of the output (false)
- `camera.move` (writes): Keys a preset camera move round `target` (an object or a point) from frame `start` for `duration` frames, turning to aim at the target, as one undo step: pushIn (dolly in by `amount`), pushHover (push in 18 frames swinging `yaw` and `tilt`, hover creeping in, settle back), orbit (`degrees` round at constant speed, `easeEnds` only at the ends), craneRise (from close and low, `scale` 3 to 1, rise and pull back to where the camera is), reveal (from a close-up out to where the camera is), pullBack (out by `amount`), whip (a fast pan to `to`, turning motion blur on), follow (keeps an `offset` from a moving object, aimed `lead` seconds ahead, lagging by `smoothing` seconds), zoomThrough (straight in to the target's surface, the distance shrinking in log space so the approach looks steady; `through` arrives at full speed with the surface's colour filling the frame), pullOut (the reverse: from filling the frame with the surface back out to a wide shot). Moves start where the camera is and as it looks at `start` (`from: "current"`), so they chain into one continuous take; `position` builds the move round that place instead. Optional `lens` to reach and `ease` [x1, y1, x2, y2]. Eases are baked as one linear key per frame.
  - `amount` number, pushIn: share of the distance closed (0.3); pushHover: share closed by the push (0.22); pullBack: how many times farther it ends (1.6)
  - `camera` integer or string, The camera; the scene's camera when left out
  - `creep` number, pushHover: share of the distance it drifts in while hovering, 0 to 0.015 (0.015)
  - `degrees` number, orbit: degrees round the target, counter-clockwise seen from above; negative turns clockwise (90)
  - `distance` number, pullOut: metres from the target to the wide shot it ends on, back along the camera's line of sight (the camera's distance, or 8 times the target's half-size when it is closer than its size)
  - `duration` number, Frames the move takes, 1 to 10000 (pushIn 45, pushHover 90, orbit 90, craneRise 110, reveal 60, pullBack 45, whip 10, follow 90)
  - `ease` number[], A cubic-bezier [x1, y1, x2, y2] instead of the preset's main ease (x1 and x2 from 0 to 1)
  - `easeEnds` string, one of `none` | `in` | `out` | `inOut`, orbit: speed up and slow down only at the ends (none: constant speed throughout)
  - `from` string, one of `current` | `position`, Where the move starts: current, where the camera is and how it looks at `start` (the default), so moves chain without a jump; position, round `position` aimed at the target from the first frame (the default when `position` is given)
  - `gap` number, zoomThrough and pullOut: metres from the surface where the move ends or starts (1.5 times the camera's near clipping distance)
  - `height` number, orbit: height above the target in metres (where the camera is)
  - `lead` number, follow: seconds ahead of the object the camera aims, 0 to 10 (0.1)
  - `lens` number, Focal length in millimetres to reach by the end, 1 to 5000 (unchanged)
  - `motionBlur` boolean, whip: turn the scene's motion blur on with a 0.5-frame shutter (true); it shows in path-traced renders
  - `offset` number[], follow: where the camera keeps to, from the object's centre, in metres (the camera's offset at `start`) [x, y, z]
  - `position` number[], Where the camera is, instead of where it is at `start` (implies `from: "position"`) [x, y, z]
  - `preset` string, required, one of `pushIn` | `pushHover` | `orbit` | `craneRise` | `reveal` | `pullBack` | `whip` | `follow` | `zoomThrough` | `pullOut`, The move
  - `radius` number, orbit: horizontal distance from the target in metres (where the camera is)
  - `rise` number, craneRise: degrees the camera rises over the target (25)
  - `scale` number, craneRise and reveal: how many times larger the target looks at the start (3, 2.5)
  - `smoothing` number, follow: seconds the camera lags behind (a critically damped spring), 0 to 10; 0 sticks rigidly (0.3)
  - `start` number, The first frame of the move (the current frame)
  - `target` integer or string or array, What the camera looks at and moves around (required, except for whip from where the camera is); follow: the object it follows
  - `through` boolean, zoomThrough: arrive at full speed instead of slowing to rest, for a cut on the colour that fills the frame (false)
  - `tilt` number, pushHover: degrees it rises during the push (8)
  - `to` integer or string or array, whip: what the camera swings to
  - `yaw` number, pushHover: degrees the camera swings round the target during the push (34)
- `camera.shake` (writes): Adds a decaying shake on top of the camera's keys from `frame` on (nothing before), as one undo step: jolts of `amplitude` metres and `rotation` degrees at `frequency` per second, dying away at `decay` per second; seeded noise, so the same `seed` gives the same shake. Run it after the camera moves it rides on.
  - `amplitude` number, Metres the camera jolts sideways and up at first, 0 to 10 (0.03)
  - `camera` integer or string, The camera; the scene's camera when left out
  - `decay` number, How fast it dies away, per second: the strength falls by e every 1/decay seconds, 0.1 to 1000 (9)
  - `frame` number, The frame the shake hits, at full strength (the current frame)
  - `frequency` number, Jolts per second, 0.1 to 120 (14)
  - `rotation` number, Degrees it jolts in pitch and yaw at first (half that in roll), 0 to 45 (0.6)
  - `seed` integer, Picks a different, repeatable shake (0)
- `camera.handheld` (writes): Adds a slow handheld float on top of the camera's keys from `start` to `end`, as one undo step: two sine sways of `period` seconds (2.7 and 4.1) up to `amount` metres and `rotation` degrees, fading to exactly nothing inside each of `holds` ([[first, last], ...]) and at its ends over 6 frames. Run it after the camera moves it rides on.
  - `amount` number, Metres the camera drifts at most along its own right and up, 0 to 10 (0.01)
  - `camera` integer or string, The camera; the scene's camera when left out
  - `end` number, The last frame of the float (the scene's last frame)
  - `holds` array[], Frame ranges [[first, last], ...] where the camera is dead still; the float fades out over the 6 frames before each and back in over the 6 after
  - `period` number or array, How slowly it sways: two sine waves added together ([2.7, 4.1] seconds)
  - `rotation` number, Degrees it drifts at most in pitch and yaw (half that in roll), 0 to 45 (0.25)
  - `seed` integer, Picks a different, repeatable sway (0)
  - `start` number, The first frame of the float (the scene's first frame)
- `light.studio` (writes): Builds or updates a three-point light rig on `target` as one undo step: Key Light (a spot camera-left), Fill Light (a cool area light), Rim Light (a warm spot from behind), named so they can be edited; sets the world strength, ambient occlusion, and the AgX view. `preset` product, dramatic, or soft; `distance` in metres.
  - `distance` number, Metres from the target to the key and rim lights (five times half the target's largest side, at least 1)
  - `preset` string, one of `product` | `dramatic` | `soft`, The rig's mood (product)
  - `target` integer or string or array, required, What the lights point at
- `object.drop` (writes): Keys `objects` falling in from `height` metres above where they rest at `start`, accelerating as under gravity over `duration` frames, with an optional `bounce` and a stretch, squash and settle as they land, as one undo step.
  - `bounce` number, Height of the bounce as a share of the fall, 0 to 0.5 (0.12; 0 for none)
  - `duration` number, Frames the fall takes, 1 to 10000 (12)
  - `height` number, Metres above where they rest that they fall from (2)
  - `objects` integer or string or array, The objects; the selection when left out
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
  - `squash` boolean, Stretch as they land, squash and settle (scale 1.06, 0.97, 1 over 4 frames) (true)
  - `start` number, The frame the fall starts (the current frame)
- `object.hop` (writes): Keys `objects` hopping on a ballistic arc from where they are at `start` to `to` (a point for their centre, or an object to land on top of) over `duration` frames, rising `height` above the higher end, with optional `spin` degrees, landing with a squash that rings out (`impact` {squash, frames}), as one undo step. Answers the landing frame.
  - `duration` number, Frames in the air, 1 to 10000 (18)
  - `height` number, Metres the arc rises above the higher of its two ends, 0 to 10000 (0.6)
  - `impact` boolean or object, The squash and stretch as they land ({squash: 0.12, frames: 8})
  - `objects` integer or string or array, The objects; the selection when left out. They hop together, keeping their places relative to one another
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
  - `spin` number[], Degrees they turn about X, Y and Z in the air [x, y, z]
  - `start` number, The frame they take off (the current frame)
  - `to` integer or string or array, required, Where they land: a point their centre lands on, or an object they land on top of
- `object.gather` (writes): Keys `objects` swirling in from where they are at `start` to an evenly spaced ring of `radius` round `center` (0: a cluster just touching), each on a spiral that turns `arc` degrees on the way, `stagger` frames apart (shrinking gaps with `accelerate`), each over `duration` frames, as one undo step.
  - `accelerate` boolean, The gaps shrink from `stagger` to `minStagger`, so they come faster and faster (false)
  - `arc` number, Degrees each swirls round the centre on the way, counter-clockwise seen from above; negative turns clockwise (90)
  - `center` integer or string or array, required, What they gather round: a point, or an object's bounding-box centre
  - `duration` number, Frames each takes, 1 to 10000 (30)
  - `level` number, Height in metres of the ring (each keeps its own height)
  - `minStagger` number, accelerate: the last gap in frames (0.2)
  - `objects` integer or string or array, The objects, in the order they set off; the selection when left out
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
  - `radius` number, Metres from the centre to the ring they end on, 0 to 10000; 0 packs them into a cluster just touching (half their mean distance from the centre)
  - `spin` number[], Degrees each turns about X, Y and Z on the way [x, y, z]
  - `stagger` number, Frames between one setting off and the next (2; 4 with accelerate)
  - `start` number, The frame the first sets off (the current frame)
- `object.wave` (writes): Keys a wave running out from `origin` at `speed` metres a second over `objects`, as one undo step: as it reaches each one (by its distance), it bumps in size by `amount` (property scale) or switches its own material's base colour to `color` and leaves it there (property color), over `duration` frames. Separate objects only, not an Array modifier's copies.
  - `amount` number, scale: how much larger at the top of the bump, -0.9 to 100 (0.25)
  - `color` array or string, color: the colour each switches to (#rrggbb or linear [r, g, b])
  - `duration` number, Frames each object's bump or switch takes, 1 to 10000 (10)
  - `objects` integer or string or array, The objects; the selection when left out
  - `origin` integer or string or array, required, Where the wave starts: a point, or an object's bounding-box centre
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
  - `property` string, one of `scale` | `color`, What the wave does: scale, a bump in size; color, switches each one's material base colour to `color` and leaves it there (scale)
  - `speed` number, Metres a second the wave travels, 0.001 to 100000 (4)
  - `start` number, The frame the wave sets off from `origin` (the current frame)
- `object.pop` (writes): Keys `objects` growing from nothing to their size with an overshoot over `duration` frames, one after another `stagger` frames apart (shrinking gaps with `accelerate`), as one undo step.
  - `accelerate` boolean, The gaps shrink from `stagger` to `minStagger`, so they come faster and faster (false)
  - `duration` number, Frames each takes to grow, 1 to 10000 (12)
  - `minStagger` number, accelerate: the last gap in frames (0.2)
  - `objects` integer or string or array, The objects, in the order they pop; the selection when left out
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
  - `stagger` number, Frames between one starting and the next (3; 4 with accelerate)
  - `start` number, The frame the first one starts (the current frame)

### Add > Mesh

- `add.plane` (writes): Adds a plane mesh of `size` at `location` (with rotation, scale and `name`) and answers its name and object id; name it to address it in the same run.
  - `location` number[], Where to put it, in metres (the origin when left out) [x, y, z]
  - `name` string, The object's name
  - `rotation` number[], Rotation in degrees, XYZ Euler [x, y, z]
  - `scale` number[], Scale [x, y, z]
  - `size` number, Side length in metres (2)
- `add.backdrop` (writes): Adds a backdrop (a cyclorama): a floor curving up into a wall, smooth, so renders show no horizon. `width`, `depth` (floor in front of the curve, centred on the origin), `height`, and `radius` in metres, `segments` round the curve.
  - `depth` number, Depth of the floor in front of the curve in metres, centred on the origin (10)
  - `height` number, Height of the wall in metres (8)
  - `location` number[], Where to put it, in metres (the origin when left out) [x, y, z]
  - `name` string, The object's name
  - `radius` number, Radius of the curve from floor to wall in metres (3)
  - `rotation` number[], Rotation in degrees, XYZ Euler [x, y, z]
  - `scale` number[], Scale [x, y, z]
  - `segments` integer, Faces round the curve, 1 to 256 (16)
  - `width` number, Width across X in metres (20)
- `add.cube` (writes): Adds a cube mesh of `size` at `location` (with rotation, scale and `name`) and answers its name and object id; name it to address it in the same run.
  - `location` number[], Where to put it, in metres (the origin when left out) [x, y, z]
  - `name` string, The object's name
  - `rotation` number[], Rotation in degrees, XYZ Euler [x, y, z]
  - `scale` number[], Scale [x, y, z]
  - `size` number, Side length in metres (2)
- `add.circle` (writes): Adds a circle mesh of `radius` and vertex count, optionally filled at `location` (with rotation, scale and `name`) and answers its name and object id; name it to address it in the same run.
  - `fill` string, one of `nothing` | `ngon` | `triangleFan`, How to fill it
  - `location` number[], Where to put it, in metres (the origin when left out) [x, y, z]
  - `name` string, The object's name
  - `radius` number, Radius in metres (1)
  - `rotation` number[], Rotation in degrees, XYZ Euler [x, y, z]
  - `scale` number[], Scale [x, y, z]
  - `vertices` integer, Vertices (32)
- `add.uvSphere` (writes): Adds a UV sphere mesh of `radius` with segments and rings at `location` (with rotation, scale and `name`) and answers its name and object id; name it to address it in the same run.
  - `location` number[], Where to put it, in metres (the origin when left out) [x, y, z]
  - `name` string, The object's name
  - `radius` number, Radius in metres (1)
  - `rings` integer, Rings from pole to pole (16)
  - `rotation` number[], Rotation in degrees, XYZ Euler [x, y, z]
  - `scale` number[], Scale [x, y, z]
  - `segments` integer, Segments around (32)
- `add.icoSphere` (writes): Adds a icosphere mesh of `radius` and subdivision level at `location` (with rotation, scale and `name`) and answers its name and object id; name it to address it in the same run.
  - `location` number[], Where to put it, in metres (the origin when left out) [x, y, z]
  - `name` string, The object's name
  - `radius` number, Radius in metres (1)
  - `rotation` number[], Rotation in degrees, XYZ Euler [x, y, z]
  - `scale` number[], Scale [x, y, z]
  - `subdivisions` integer, Subdivisions, 1 to 8 (2)
- `add.cylinder` (writes): Adds a cylinder mesh of `radius` and `depth` at `location` (with rotation, scale and `name`) and answers its name and object id; name it to address it in the same run.
  - `depth` number, Height in metres (2)
  - `fill` string, one of `nothing` | `ngon` | `triangleFan`, How the ends are closed
  - `location` number[], Where to put it, in metres (the origin when left out) [x, y, z]
  - `name` string, The object's name
  - `radius` number, Radius in metres (1)
  - `rotation` number[], Rotation in degrees, XYZ Euler [x, y, z]
  - `scale` number[], Scale [x, y, z]
  - `vertices` integer, Vertices around (32)
- `add.cone` (writes): Adds a cone mesh with bottom and top radii and `depth` at `location` (with rotation, scale and `name`) and answers its name and object id; name it to address it in the same run.
  - `depth` number, Height in metres (2)
  - `fill` string, one of `nothing` | `ngon` | `triangleFan`, How the ends are closed
  - `location` number[], Where to put it, in metres (the origin when left out) [x, y, z]
  - `name` string, The object's name
  - `radius1` number, Bottom radius in metres (1)

  - `rotation` number[], Rotation in degrees, XYZ Euler [x, y, z]
  - `scale` number[], Scale [x, y, z]
  - `vertices` integer, Vertices around (32)
- `add.torus` (writes): Adds a torus mesh with major and minor radii and segments at `location` (with rotation, scale and `name`) and answers its name and object id; name it to address it in the same run.
  - `location` number[], Where to put it, in metres (the origin when left out) [x, y, z]

  - `minorRadius` number, Tube radius in metres (0.25)
  - `minorSegments` integer, Segments around the tube (12)

  - `scale` number[], Scale [x, y, z]
- `add.grid` (writes): Adds a grid mesh of `size` with x and y subdivisions at `location` (with rotation, scale and `name`) and answers its name and object id; name it to address it in the same run.
  - `location` number[], Where to put it, in metres (the origin when left out) [x, y, z]
  - `name` string, The object's name
  - `rotation` number[], Rotation in degrees, XYZ Euler [x, y, z]
  - `scale` number[], Scale [x, y, z]

### Add

- `add.light` (writes): Adds a light (point, sun, spot or area) with color and power at `location` (with rotation, scale and `name`) and answers its name and object id; name it to address it in the same run.

- `add.empty` (writes): Adds a empty (an axis marker for parenting and targets) at `location` (with rotation, scale and `name`) and answers its name and object id; name it to address it in the same run.

- `add.text` (writes): Adds a text object with `body` and `size` at `location` and answers its name and object id.

### Object > Transform

- `object.transform` (writes): Sets location, rotation (degrees) and/or scale of `objects` (names or ids; the selection without it) absolutely.
  - `location` number[], Location in metres [x, y, z]
  - `objects` integer or string or array, The objects; the selection when left out
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
  - `rotation` number[], Rotation in degrees, XYZ Euler [x, y, z]
  - `scale` number[], Scale [x, y, z]
- `object.translate` (writes): Moves `objects` (names or ids; the selection without it) by `offset` [x, y, z].
  - `objects` integer or string or array, The objects; the selection when left out
  - `offset` number[], required, How far, in metres [x, y, z]
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
- `object.rotate` (writes): Rotates `objects` (names or ids; the selection without it) by `angle` degrees about `axis` (x, y or z).
  - `angle` number, required, Degrees, counter-clockwise looking down the axis
  - `axis` string, required, one of `x` | `y` | `z`, The world axis to turn about
  - `objects` integer or string or array, The objects; the selection when left out
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
- `object.scale` (writes): Scales `objects` (names or ids; the selection without it) by `factor` (a number or [x, y, z]).
  - `factor` number or array, required, A number, or [x, y, z]
  - `objects` integer or string or array, The objects; the selection when left out
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
- `object.lookAt` (writes): Rotates `object` so it points at `target` [x, y, z] (cameras and lights look along -Z).
  - `object` integer or string, The object to turn (a camera or a light); the active one when left out
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
  - `target` number[], required, The point to look at, in metres [x, y, z]

### Object > Apply

- `object.applyTransform` (writes): Bakes the location, rotation and/or scale of `objects` (names or ids; the selection without it) into the mesh data and resets them.
  - `location` boolean, Apply the location (false)
  - `objects` integer or string or array, The objects; the selection when left out
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
  - `rotation` boolean, Apply the rotation (true)
  - `scale` boolean, Apply the scale (true)

  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
- `object.reveal` (writes): Shows `objects` (names or ids; the selection without it) again, or every hidden object without it.
  - `objects` integer or string or array, The hidden objects to show; every hidden object when left out
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)

### Mesh > Select Mode

- `mesh.selectVertexMode` (reads): Switches edit mode to vertex selection. No parameters.
- `mesh.selectEdgeMode` (reads): Switches edit mode to edge selection. No parameters.
- `mesh.selectFaceMode` (reads): Switches edit mode to face selection. No parameters.

### Mesh

- `mesh.extrude` (writes): Extrudes the selected faces (or loose vertices and edges) along their normals by `distance`, plus `offset`, in edit mode on the edited mesh's selected elements (`mode.set {mode: "edit"}` and `mesh.select` first).
  - `distance` number, How far along the faces' mean normal, in metres (1)
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
  - `offset` number[], An extra offset in metres [x, y, z]
- `mesh.inset` (writes): Insets the selected faces by `thickness`, in edit mode on the edited mesh's selected elements (`mode.set {mode: "edit"}` and `mesh.select` first).
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
  - `thickness` number, How far in, in metres (0.1)
- `mesh.bevel` (writes): Bevels the selected edges with `width` and `segments`, in edit mode on the edited mesh's selected elements (`mode.set {mode: "edit"}` and `mesh.select` first).
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
  - `segments` integer, Segments across the bevel (1)
  - `width` number, The bevel's width in metres (0.1)
- `mesh.subdivide` (writes): Subdivides the selected edges and faces, in edit mode on the edited mesh's selected elements (`mode.set {mode: "edit"}` and `mesh.select` first).
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
- `mesh.loopCut` (writes): Adds `cuts` edge loops across the ring of edge `edge` [vertex, vertex] at `factor` in the edited mesh.
  - `cuts` integer, Number of loops (1)
  - `edge` integer[], required, The edge the cut crosses, as [vertex, vertex]
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
  - `factor` number, Where a single loop goes between the sides, 0 to 1 (0.5)
- `mesh.merge` (writes): Merges the selected vertices at their centre, in edit mode on the edited mesh's selected elements (`mode.set {mode: "edit"}` and `mesh.select` first).
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
- `mesh.fill` (writes): Makes a face from the vertices in `vertices` (else the selection) of the edited mesh.
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
  - `vertices` integer[], The face's corners in order; the selection when left out
- `mesh.bridge` (writes): Bridges two selected edge loops with faces, in edit mode on the edited mesh's selected elements (`mode.set {mode: "edit"}` and `mesh.select` first).
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
- `mesh.bisect` (writes): Cuts the whole edited mesh, whatever is selected, along the plane through `point` (the selection's centre when left out) with `normal`, optionally filling the cut and clearing one side.
  - `clearInner` boolean, Delete what lies behind the plane
  - `clearOuter` boolean, Delete what lies in front of the plane
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
  - `fill` boolean, Close the cut with a face (with clearing)
  - `normal` number[], The plane's normal, in the object's own axes ([0, 0, 1]) [x, y, z]
  - `point` number[], A point on the cutting plane, in the object's own axes (the selection's centre) [x, y, z]
- `mesh.separate` (writes): Moves the selected elements of the edited mesh into a new object named `name`.
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
  - `name` string, The new object's name
- `mesh.spin` (writes): Spins the selected elements `angle` degrees about `axis` through `center` in `steps`, making a lathe.
  - `angle` number, Degrees to sweep (90); 360 closes the sweep
  - `axis` number[], The axis to sweep round ([0, 0, 1]) [x, y, z]
  - `center` number[], A point on the axis, in the object's own axes (the origin) [x, y, z]
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
  - `steps` integer, Steps (12)
- `mesh.bevelVertices` (writes): Bevels the selected vertices with `width`, in edit mode on the edited mesh's selected elements (`mode.set {mode: "edit"}` and `mesh.select` first).
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
  - `width` number, How far along each edge the cut is, metres (0.1)
- `mesh.proportional` (reads): Turns proportional editing on or off and sets its falloff and radius; answers the setting.
  - `connected` boolean, Only vertices joined to the selection by edges follow, by their distance along the edges
  - `falloff` string, one of `smooth` | `sphere` | `root` | `linear` | `sharp` | `constant`, How the pull fades with distance
  - `on` boolean, On or off; toggles when left out
  - `radius` number, How far, in metres, unselected vertices follow (1)
- `mesh.knife` (writes): Cuts the edited mesh along `points` (screen-space path), through the whole mesh with `through`.
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
  - `points` json[], The cut line: view pixels [x, y], or points in the world [x, y, z], at least two
  - `through` boolean, Cut faces turned away from the view too (false)
- `mesh.edgeSlide` (writes): Slides the selected edges along their neighbours by `factor` (-1 to 1), in edit mode on the edited mesh's selected elements (`mode.set {mode: "edit"}` and `mesh.select` first).
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
  - `factor` number, required, How far towards the next edge loop, -1 to 1

### Mesh > Delete

- `mesh.deleteFaces` (writes): Deletes the selected faces, in edit mode on the edited mesh's selected elements (`mode.set {mode: "edit"}` and `mesh.select` first).
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
- `mesh.deleteVertices` (writes): Deletes the selected vertices and the faces using them, in edit mode on the edited mesh's selected elements (`mode.set {mode: "edit"}` and `mesh.select` first).
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)

### Mesh > Normals

- `mesh.flip` (writes): Flips the normals of the selected faces, in edit mode on the edited mesh's selected elements (`mode.set {mode: "edit"}` and `mesh.select` first).
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
- `mesh.recalculateNormals` (writes): Recalculates the normals of `objects` (names or ids; the selection without it) so they point outside.
  - `objects` integer or string or array, Object mode: the mesh objects to turn outward; the selection when left out. Edit mode works on the edited mesh
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)

### Mesh > Transform

- `mesh.translate` (writes): Moves the selected elements by `offset`, in edit mode on the edited mesh's selected elements (`mode.set {mode: "edit"}` and `mesh.select` first).
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
  - `offset` number[], required, How far in the object's own axes, in metres [x, y, z]
- `mesh.scale` (writes): Scales the selected elements by `factor` about `pivot`, in edit mode on the edited mesh's selected elements (`mode.set {mode: "edit"}` and `mesh.select` first).
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
  - `factor` number or array, required, A number, or [x, y, z]
  - `pivot` number[], The point to scale about; the selection's centre when left out [x, y, z]
- `mesh.rotate` (writes): Rotates the selected elements by `angle` degrees about `axis` through `pivot`, in edit mode on the edited mesh's selected elements (`mode.set {mode: "edit"}` and `mesh.select` first).
  - `angle` number, required, Degrees, counter-clockwise looking down the axis
  - `axis` string, required, one of `x` | `y` | `z`, The object's axis to turn round
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
  - `pivot` number[], The point to turn about; the selection's centre when left out [x, y, z]

### Modifier

- `modifier.add` (writes): Adds a modifier (subdivision, mirror, array, bevel, solidify, boolean, displace, …) with its settings to `object`.
  - `angle` number, screw: degrees to turn
  - `angleLimit` number, bevel: edges sharper than this many degrees are bevelled; decimate planar: faces flatter than this join (5)
  - `axes` boolean[], mirror: [x, y, z] axes to mirror across
  - `axis` string, one of `x` | `y` | `z`, screw and simpleDeform: the local axis
  - `constantOffset` number[], array: an extra offset in metres [x, y, z]
  - `coordinates` string, one of `local` | `global` | `uv`, displace: where the image is looked up (local: -1 to 1 in object axes covers it once)
  - `count` integer, array: the number of copies
  - `direction` string, one of `normal` | `x` | `y` | `z`, displace: where to push
  - `distance` number, weld: the distance that joins vertices
  - `envelopes` boolean, armature: vertices in no bone's group follow the bones whose envelopes reach them (false)
  - `factor` number, smooth: how far each vertex moves towards its neighbours
  - `group` integer, geometryNodes: the node group's id (nodes.newGroup makes one)
  - `image` string, displace: an image's hash (from image.add) whose brightness pushes; null for none
  - `inputs` object, geometryNodes: the group's inputs by name
  - `invertVertexGroup` boolean, armature: use one minus that group's weights
  - `iterations` integer, decimate unsubdivide: half steps of subdivision to undo, 0 to 16
  - `levels` integer, subdivision: levels, 0 to 6; multires: the level shown (at most the mesh's levels)
  - `limits` number[], simpleDeform: [low, high], the share of the range that deforms, 0 to 1
  - `merge` boolean, mirror and array: join vertices where copies meet
  - `mergeThreshold` number, mirror: the distance that joins vertices on the plane
  - `midLevel` number, displace: the value that does not move (0.5)
  - `mode` string, one of `twist` | `bend` | `taper` | `stretch` | `collapse` | `unsubdivide` | `planar`, simpleDeform: what it does; decimate: collapse, unsubdivide, or planar
  - `multiModifier` boolean, armature: deform what the Armature modifier above got and mix over its result by the group
  - `negative` boolean, shrinkwrap project: cast against it (false)
  - `noiseScale` number, displace: noise feature size in metres; 0 pushes every vertex alike
  - `object` integer or string, The mesh object; the active one when left out
  - `offset` number, solidify: -1 grows inwards, 1 outwards; wireframe: -1 to 1; shrinkwrap: metres kept from the surface
  - `operand` integer or string, boolean and shrinkwrap: the other mesh object; lattice: the lattice object; armature: the armature
  - `operation` string, one of `difference` | `union` | `intersect`, boolean: what to keep
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
  - `positive` boolean, shrinkwrap project: cast along the vertex normal (true)
  - `preserveVolume` boolean, armature: blend the bones as dual quaternions, so joints keep their volume (false)
  - `ratio` number, decimate collapse: the share of triangles to keep, 0 to 1
  - `relativeOffset` number[], array: the offset between copies as a fraction of the mesh size [x, y, z]
  - `rim` boolean, solidify: close the open edges
  - `screwOffset` number, screw: how far along the axis one turn moves, metres
  - `sculptLevels` integer, multires: the level sculpt mode shows and sculpts
  - `segments` integer, bevel: segments across each bevel (1 is a flat chamfer)
  - `steps` integer, screw: steps around one turn
  - `strength` number, displace: how far, in metres, at full value; lattice: how much of the bend (1)
  - `thickness` number, solidify: the shell's thickness in metres
  - `type` string, required, one of `mirror` | `array` | `subdivision` | `solidify` | `triangulate` | `weld` | `smooth` | `bevel` | `boolean` | `screw` | `displace` | `decimate` | `wireframe` | `simpleDeform` | `cast` | `multires` | `shrinkwrap` | `lattice` | `geometryNodes`, The modifier
  - `vertexGroup` string, armature: a group whose weights say how much of the deformation each vertex takes; null for all
  - `vertexGroups` boolean, armature: vertices follow the bones of their groups (true)
  - `width` number, bevel: the bevel's width in metres
  - `wrapMethod` string, one of `nearestSurface` | `project` | `nearestVertex`, shrinkwrap: where vertices go

### Material

- `material.new` (writes): Creates a material with base color, metallic and roughness and answers its id. It is given to the selected objects (in Edit mode, to the object edited) unless `assign: false`; the answer lists them.
  - `assign` boolean, Give it to the selected objects: true unless false
  - `baseColor` array or string, Base colour
  - `metallic` number, 0 to 1
  - `name` string, The material's name
  - `roughness` number, 0 to 1
- `material.clear` (writes): Removes the materials from `objects` (names or ids; the selection without it).
  - `objects` integer or string or array, The objects; the selection when left out
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)

### Render

- `world.set` (writes): Sets the world background color and strength, rotation and volume.
  - `color` array or string, Background colour
  - `rotation` number, Degrees the world image is turned about the up axis
  - `strength` number, How strongly it (or its image) lights the scene
  - `volume` integer or string or null, A shader group (id or name) whose Volume fills the world in path-traced renders, or null for none
- `render.set` (writes): Sets render width and height, motion blur and shutter, ambient occlusion (on, distance, strength), and colour management (view transform, look, exposure).
  - `ao` boolean, Ambient occlusion in fast renders: creases and covered places get less of the world's light (on)
  - `aoDistance` number or null, How far around a point surfaces occlude it, in metres (up to 1000); null works it out from the scene's size (6 % of its diagonal, 0.05 to 2 m)
  - `aoStrength` number, How much of the occlusion shows, 0 to 4 (1)
  - `exposure` number, Stops of exposure before the view transform, -32 to 32 (0)
  - `height` integer, Pixels
  - `look` string, one of `none` | `punchy` | `greyscale` | `high-contrast` | `low-contrast`, A grade after the view transform (none)
  - `motionBlur` boolean, Blur what moves while the shutter is open, in path-traced renders
  - `shutter` number, How long the shutter is open, in frames (0.5)
  - `shutterPosition` string, one of `center` | `start` | `end`, Where the shutter opens around the frame (center)
  - `view` string, one of `standard` | `agx` | `khronos-pbr-neutral`, Colour management's view transform (standard): standard clips at white, agx and khronos-pbr-neutral roll highlights off
  - `width` integer, Pixels
- `render.image` (reads): Renders the active camera's view (at `frame`, with `samples`) and answers it as a base64 PNG with its size. Does not change the scene.
  - `frame` number, The frame to render (the current frame when left out)
  - `samples` integer, Samples per pixel side, 1 to 4 (2)
- `world.setImage` (writes): Sets an environment image (workspace path or base64) as the world background, with rotation and strength, or clears it.
  - `base64` string, The image's bytes, instead of a path
  - `clear` boolean, Remove the image: the world colour shows and lights again
  - `name` string, The image's name, with base64
  - `path` file, An equirectangular .hdr, .png, or .jpg, relative to this scene's folder
  - `rotation` number, Degrees the image is turned about the up axis
  - `strength` number, How strongly the world lights the scene
- `render.trace.start` (reads): Starts a path-traced render (bounces, samples, denoise) in steps; answers its progress. Continue with `render.trace.step`.
  - `bounces` integer, The longest light path, in bounces (4)
  - `collect` boolean, Trace nothing here: merge the sums of workers' shards (false)
  - `denoise` boolean, Smooth the remaining noise away (false)
  - `frame` number, The frame to render; the current frame when left out
  - `samples` integer, Samples per pixel, 1 to 4096 (64)
  - `seed` integer, Changes the noise pattern (0)
  - `volumeBounces` integer, How often light may scatter in a volume before the path ends (0: each point in a volume is lit directly only)
  - `wait` boolean, Render to the end and answer the image at once (false)
- `frame.range` (writes): Sets the animation's start and end frames and frames per second.
  - `end` integer, The last frame
  - `fps` number, Frames per second
  - `start` integer, The first frame
- `render.animation` (reads): Renders frames `start` to `end` (every `step`) and answers them as pictures. Does not change the scene.
  - `end` integer, The last frame (the range's end when left out)
  - `samples` integer, Samples per pixel side, 1 to 4 (1)
  - `start` integer, The first frame (the range's start when left out)
  - `step` integer, Render every nth frame (1)
- `compositor.new` (writes): Creates a compositing node group and uses it for renders when `use`.
  - `name` string, The group's name (Compositing when left out)
  - `use` boolean, Make renders pass through it (true)

### File

- `file.export` (reads): Exports the scene (or `selectedOnly`) as glTF/GLB, OBJ, STL, FBX, USD (usda, usdc, usdz) or a PNG render and answers the file as base64. Does not change the scene.
  - `format` string, required, one of `glb` | `gltf` | `obj` | `stl` | `fbx` | `usda` | `usdc` | `usdz` | `png`, The file format
  - `frame` number, png: the frame to render (the current frame when left out)
  - `samples` integer, png: samples per pixel side, 1 to 4 (2)
  - `selectedOnly` boolean, Only the selected objects
- `file.import` (writes): Imports a glTF/GLB, OBJ, STL, FBX, USD or .blend file from the workspace (`path`) or base64 into the scene.
  - `base64` string, The file's bytes, instead of a path
  - `format` string, one of `glb` | `gltf` | `obj` | `stl` | `fbx` | `usd` | `usda` | `usdc` | `usdz` | `blend`, The format of base64 bytes
  - `path` file, A .glb, .gltf, .obj, .stl, .fbx, .usd, .usda, .usdc, .usdz, or .blend file, relative to this scene's folder

### View > Shading

- `view.wireframe` (reads): Sets the viewport shading to wireframe. No parameters.
- `view.solid` (reads): Sets the viewport shading to solid. No parameters.
- `view.material` (reads): Sets the viewport shading to material preview. No parameters.
- `view.rendered` (reads): Shows progressive path tracing of the viewport with scene lights, materials and editor overlays. No parameters.

### View > Viewpoint

- `view.front` (reads): Looks at the scene from the front. No parameters.
- `view.right` (reads): Looks at the scene from the right. No parameters.
- `view.top` (reads): Looks at the scene from the top. No parameters.
- `view.camera` (reads): Looks through the active camera. No parameters.

### View

- `view.perspective` (reads): Toggles the viewport between perspective and orthographic. No parameters.
- `view.frameAll` (reads): Frames every object in the viewport. No parameters.
- `view.frameSelected` (reads): Frames the selected objects in the viewport. No parameters.
- `view.grid` (reads): Shows or hides the grid floor in the viewport.
  - `on` boolean, Show the grid; toggles when left out
- `view.overlays` (reads): Shows or hides every overlay: the grid, lights, cameras, empties, origins, outlines and edit marks, so the viewport (a rendered camera view too) shows only the scene.
  - `on` boolean, Show the overlays; toggles when left out

### Mesh > Extrude

- `mesh.extrudeIndividual` (writes): Extrudes each selected face separately along its own normal by `distance`, in edit mode on the edited mesh's selected elements (`mode.set {mode: "edit"}` and `mesh.select` first).
  - `distance` number, How far each face moves along its own normal, metres (1)
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)

### Mesh > Dissolve

- `mesh.dissolveVertices` (writes): Dissolves the selected vertices, merging the faces around them, in edit mode on the edited mesh's selected elements (`mode.set {mode: "edit"}` and `mesh.select` first).
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
- `mesh.dissolveEdges` (writes): Dissolves the selected edges, merging the faces on both sides, in edit mode on the edited mesh's selected elements (`mode.set {mode: "edit"}` and `mesh.select` first).
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
- `mesh.dissolveFaces` (writes): Dissolves the selected faces into one face, in edit mode on the edited mesh's selected elements (`mode.set {mode: "edit"}` and `mesh.select` first).
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)

### Mesh > Mirror

- `mesh.symmetrize` (writes): Makes the whole edited mesh, whatever is selected, symmetric across `axis`, copying one side to the other.
  - `axis` string, one of `x` | `y` | `z`, The axis whose plane the mesh is mirrored across (x)
  - `direction` string, one of `positive` | `negative`, Which side replaces the other (positive)
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)

### Mesh > UV

- `uv.smartProject` (writes): Unwraps `objects` (names or ids; the selection without it) with smart UV project (by angle limit, with margin).
  - `angleLimit` number, Faces whose normals differ by more than this many degrees go to separate islands (66)
  - `margin` number, Space between islands, as a fraction of the texture (0.02)
  - `objects` integer or string or array, The mesh objects, in object mode; the selection when left out
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
- `uv.cubeProject` (writes): Projects UVs of `objects` (names or ids; the selection without it) from a cube of `size`.
  - `objects` integer or string or array, The mesh objects, in object mode; the selection when left out
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
  - `size` number, Metres one repeat of the texture covers (2)
- `uv.cylinderProject` (writes): Projects UVs of `objects` (names or ids; the selection without it) from a cylinder.
  - `objects` integer or string or array, The mesh objects, in object mode; the selection when left out
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
- `uv.sphereProject` (writes): Projects UVs of `objects` (names or ids; the selection without it) from a sphere.
  - `objects` integer or string or array, The mesh objects, in object mode; the selection when left out
  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
- `uv.planarProject` (writes): Projects UVs of `objects` (names or ids; the selection without it) flat along `axis`.

A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)

- `uv.reset` (writes): Resets the UVs of `objects` (names or ids; the selection without it) so each face fills the whole UV square.

  - `pick` number[], Instead of `object`/`objects`: a world point [x, y, z] in metres; the command acts on the object there now (the smallest whose mesh's bounds hold the point, else the nearest light, camera, empty, curve, text, lattice or armature whose origin is within 0.25 m). A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
- `uv.clear` (writes): Removes the UV maps of `objects` (names or ids; the selection without it).

A place: with `basis`, a write by it is refused when what is at the point is no longer what was there (moved away, another moved in, its parent moved)
- `mesh.markSeam` (writes): Marks the selected edges as UV seams, in edit mode on the edited mesh's selected elements (`mode.set {mode: "edit"}` and `mesh.select` first).
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
- `mesh.clearSeam` (writes): Clears UV seams from the selected edges, in edit mode on the edited mesh's selected elements (`mode.set {mode: "edit"}` and `mesh.select` first).
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
- `uv.unwrap` (writes): Unwraps the edited mesh's selected faces along their seams (angle-based, conformal, or minimumStretch SLIM) with `margin`; minimum stretch uses 1 to 100 `iterations` and keeps pins fixed.
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
  - `iterations` integer, Minimum stretch iterations, 1 to 100 (30)
  - `margin` number, Space between islands, as a fraction of the square (0.02)

- `uv.liveUnwrap` (reads): Sets local UV live unwrap preferences (`on`, `method`, `iterations`) without changing the scene. Pinned UV transforms relax their islands in one undo step.
  - `iterations` integer, Minimum stretch iterations, 1 to 100 (30)
  - `method` string, one of `angleBased` | `conformal` | `minimumStretch`, Live relaxation method

- `uv.stitch` (writes): Stitches the selected UV edges to their neighbours in the UV editor.
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
- `uv.pin` (writes): Pins the selected UVs so unwrapping keeps them in place.
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)
- `uv.unpin` (writes): Unpins the selected UVs.
  - `elements` object, Runs the command in this mesh's edit mode on these elements and puts the mode and the selections back afterwards, so no `mode.set` or `mesh.select` step is needed: `object` (the mesh, an id or a name), `vertices` and `faces` (indices from 0, as `mesh.select` takes them; every vertex when both are left out)

### Object > Animation

- `anim.insertKey` (writes): Inserts keyframes for `properties` (location, rotation, scale, …) or a keying set of `objects` (names or ids; the selection without it) at `frame`.
